name: Chicken breast
notes: Lean staple. Default high-protein meat for home cooking. Values are cooked, skinless.

name: Chicken thigh (skinless)
notes: Richer flavor than breast; more fat. Hard to overcook.

name: Chicken thigh (skin on)
notes: With skin on. Crispy when roasted.

name: Turkey breast
notes: Even leaner than chicken breast. Cooked, skinless.

name: Ground chicken
notes: Cooked. Fat content varies by blend; mid-range value here.

name: Ground turkey
notes: Cooked. Common lean substitute for ground beef.

name: Ground pork
notes: Cooked. Higher fat than ground beef typically.

name: Bacon
notes: Cooked, drained. Very salty, very fatty.

name: Sausage (pork)
notes: Cooked pork sausage; values are an average across styles.

name: Hot dog (beef)
notes: Highly processed; low protein per calorie.

name: Beef jerky
notes: Dried beef. Concentrated protein and sodium.

name: Cod
notes: Mild white fish. Very lean. Cooked.

name: Pollock
notes: Mild white fish, common in processed fish. Cooked.

name: Anchovies
notes: Canned, salted. Used as a seasoning more than a main.

name: Egg (whole)
notes: Large raw egg, per 100g. Cooking changes little nutritionally.

name: Egg white
notes: Almost pure protein. Negligible fat and carbs.

name: Egg yolk
notes: All the fat and most of the flavor of the egg.

name: Romaine lettuce
notes: Crisp lettuce. Most common salad base.

name: Swiss chard
notes: Earthy leafy green with edible stems.

name: Red cabbage
notes: Sweeter and more pigmented than green cabbage.

name: Tomato
notes: Technically a fruit, used as a vegetable.

name: Red bell pepper
notes: Sweeter than green bells. High vitamin C.

name: Garlic
notes: Used in small amounts; per-100g values look high.

name: Sweet potato
notes: Cooked. More fiber and sugar than white potato.

name: Cranberry
notes: Raw. Tart; usually sweetened in use.

name: Banana
notes: Higher carb than most fresh fruits.

name: Cherry (sweet)
notes: Sweet cherries; tart varieties are lower in sugar.

name: Lemon
notes: Used in small amounts as flavoring.

name: Lentils (red)
notes: Cooked. Break down into a purée.

name: Soybeans
notes: Cooked. Unusually high protein for a plant.

name: Peanut
notes: Technically a legume, eaten like a nut. Raw.

name: Brown rice
notes: Cooked. Whole grain version of white rice.

name: Wild rice
notes: Cooked. Actually a grass seed, not rice.

name: Quinoa
notes: Cooked. Complete protein source for a plant.

name: Rolled oats
notes: Cooked. Values are for prepared oatmeal.

name: Whole wheat bread
notes: Higher fiber and protein than white bread.

name: Almond
notes: Raw. High protein for a nut.

name: Walnut
notes: Raw. Omega-3 rich for a plant.

name: Cashew
notes: Raw. Higher carbs than most nuts.

name: Pumpkin seed
notes: Very high protein for a seed.

name: White sugar
notes: Pure sucrose. Top of the carbs axis.

name: Milk chocolate
notes: Cocoa, sugar, and milk solids; classified plant-dominant for the visualization.

name: Greek yogurt (non-fat)
notes: Strained, fat removed. Very high protein per calorie.

name: Cottage cheese
notes: High-protein fresh cheese. Salt content varies.

name: Parmesan
notes: Hard aged cheese. High protein, very salty.

name: Butter
notes: Mostly saturated fat. Unsalted; salted is ~600mg sodium/100g.

name: Ice cream (vanilla)
notes: Cream and sugar; classified dairy for the visualization.

name: Chicken (whole, roasted)
notes: Mixed light and dark with skin. Values are roasted.

name: Chicken wing
notes: With skin, roasted. Fattier than breast or thigh.

name: Chicken liver
notes: Pan-fried. Dense in iron and B12.

name: Cornish hen
notes: Young small chicken, roasted with skin.

name: Goose
notes: Roasted, no skin. Skin-on values run much higher in fat.

name: Quail
notes: Cooked, no skin. Small game bird.

name: Pheasant
notes: Cooked, no skin. Lean game bird.

name: Squab
notes: Young domestic pigeon. Cooked, no skin.

name: Ostrich
notes: Cooked. Classified as poultry but eats more like lean red meat.

name: Duck leg confit
notes: Cured then slow-poached in its own fat. Very high sodium from the salt cure.

name: Beef brisket
notes: Braised or smoked. Tough cut that needs long, low cooking.

name: Beef flank steak
notes: Grilled. Lean and quick-cooking; slice thin against the grain.

name: Beef skirt steak
notes: Grilled. Loose-grained beefy cut; classic for tacos.

name: Beef shank
notes: Braised. Connective-tissue rich; gives body to broth.

name: Pork shoulder
notes: Braised or roasted. Forgiving fatty cut; shreds when fully cooked.

name: Pork belly
notes: Cooked. Layered fat and meat; the cut bacon is cured from.

name: Pork spare ribs
notes: Braised or smoked. Fatty rib section.

name: Pork tenderloin
notes: Cooked, lean only. The leanest cut of pork.

name: Lamb leg
notes: Roasted. The classic large cut for Easter or Eid roasts.

name: Lamb shank
notes: Braised. Connective-tissue rich; tender after long cooking.

name: Lamb shoulder
notes: Braised. Fattier than leg, sweeter when slow-cooked.

name: Elk
notes: Cooked. Among the leanest game red meats.

name: Rabbit
notes: Cooked. Lean white-meat game; eats more like poultry than red meat.

name: Goat
notes: Cooked. Lean red meat, common in South Asian, African, and Caribbean cooking.

name: Wild boar
notes: Cooked. Game pork; leaner and gamier than domestic pork.

name: Beef liver
notes: Pan-fried. Extremely dense in vitamin A and B12.

name: Pork liver
notes: Cooked. Sweeter and milder than beef liver.

name: Foie gras
notes: Fattened goose or duck liver. Extraordinarily fatty.

name: Beef kidney
notes: Cooked. Strong-flavored organ; classic British/French use.

name: Beef heart
notes: Cooked. Lean, dense muscle; eats like steak.

name: Beef tongue
notes: Braised then peeled. Tender and fatty.

name: Tripe
notes: Cooked. Stomach lining; requires long simmering.

name: Sweetbreads
notes: Cooked. Thymus or pancreas; mild and creamy.

name: Chorizo (Spanish)
notes: Dry-cured pork sausage with smoked paprika. Sliced like salami.

name: Chorizo (Mexican)
notes: Fresh pork sausage with vinegar and chiles. Crumbles when cooked.

name: Mortadella
notes: Bologna's Italian cousin. Studded with pork fat and sometimes pistachios.

name: Andouille
notes: Smoked Cajun pork sausage. Coarse and assertive.

name: Bratwurst
notes: German pork (and sometimes veal) sausage. Grilled or pan-fried.

name: Italian sausage
notes: Cooked. Sweet or hot pork sausage with fennel.

name: Breakfast sausage
notes: Cooked. Pork sausage seasoned with sage and pepper.

name: Pancetta
notes: Italian salt-cured pork belly. Like unsmoked bacon.

name: Pastrami
notes: Cured, spiced, smoked beef. Sliced thin.

name: Corned beef
notes: Brisket cured in salt brine. Cooked.

name: Spam
notes: Canned pork shoulder and ham. Hawaiian and Pacific staple.

name: Liverwurst
notes: Pork liver sausage. Spreadable or sliced.

name: Catfish
notes: Cooked. Sweet, mild flesh. Most US supply is farmed.

name: Grouper
notes: Cooked. Meaty Gulf and Caribbean white fish.

name: Mahi mahi
notes: Cooked. Lean tropical fish; firm pink flesh.

name: Flounder
notes: Cooked. Mild flatfish, similar to sole.

name: Herring
notes: Cooked. Oily forage fish; central to Nordic and Eastern European cuisines.

name: Tuna (skipjack)
notes: Cooked. Smaller, leaner tuna; the species in most canned 'light' tuna.

name: Carp
notes: Cooked. Oilier than other freshwater fish.

name: Striped bass
notes: Cooked. Available wild or farmed; mild and firm.

name: Canned sardines (in oil)
notes: Drained. Bones included; high in calcium.

name: Canned anchovies (in oil)
notes: Drained. Salt-cured then packed; used in tiny amounts.

name: Smoked salmon (lox)
notes: Cold-smoked. Very high sodium from the cure.

name: Salt cod (bacalao)
notes: Soaked then cooked. Still very salty even after rinsing.

name: Octopus
notes: Cooked. Lean and meaty after long braise.

name: Squid
notes: Steamed. Fried calamari has much higher fat and calories.

name: Crayfish
notes: Cooked. Very lean; common in Cajun and Nordic cooking.

name: Abalone
notes: Cooked. Prized in Chinese and Japanese cuisine; needs tenderizing.

name: Snails (escargot)
notes: Plain values; classic preparation adds garlic butter.

name: Duck egg
notes: Whole, raw. Larger and richer than chicken eggs.

name: Quail egg
notes: Whole, raw. Tiny — about a fifth the weight of a chicken egg.

name: Goose egg
notes: Whole, raw. Roughly twice the size of a chicken egg.

name: Bok choy
notes: Raw. Chinese cabbage with crisp stems.

name: Butter lettuce
notes: Raw. Soft-leaved Boston or Bibb lettuce.

name: Mustard greens
notes: Raw. Pungent and bitter; needs cooking.

name: Escarole
notes: Raw. Broad-leaved chicory; milder than endive.

name: Broccoli rabe
notes: Raw. Bitter Italian brassica also called rapini.

name: Daikon radish
notes: Raw. Large East Asian white radish.

name: Yellow squash
notes: Raw. Crookneck or straightneck summer squash.

name: Leek
notes: Raw. Mild allium; use white and pale-green parts.

name: Scallion
notes: Raw. Green onion; whole plant used.

name: Red onion
notes: Raw. Milder and sweeter than yellow.

name: Jicama
notes: Raw. Crisp, slightly sweet Mexican root.

name: Poblano
notes: Raw. Mild Mexican chili. Dried it becomes ancho.

name: Enoki mushroom
notes: Raw. Thin white mushrooms grown in clusters.

name: Sauerkraut
notes: Lacto-fermented cabbage. High sodium from the cure.

name: Kimchi
notes: Fermented Korean napa cabbage with chili and seasoning.

name: Tomato paste
notes: Concentrated tomato. Used in small spoonfuls.

name: Yukon gold potato
notes: Cooked, no skin. Buttery yellow flesh.

name: Red potato
notes: Cooked. Thin red skin; waxy flesh holds shape.

name: Cassava (yuca)
notes: Cooked. Tropical root; source of tapioca.

name: Plantain
notes: Cooked. Starchier banana relative; sugar rises as it ripens.

name: Spaghetti squash
notes: Cooked. Pulls apart into pasta-like strands.

name: Rutabaga
notes: Cooked. Cross between turnip and cabbage.

name: Mung beans
notes: Cooked. Small green bean used widely in Asia.

name: Adzuki beans
notes: Cooked. Small Asian red bean, often sweetened.

name: Black-eyed peas
notes: Cooked. Distinct eye spot; Southern US and West African staple.

name: Split peas
notes: Cooked. Yellow or green; cooks faster than whole peas.

name: Seitan
notes: Wheat gluten 'meat'. Filed under legumes for the plant-protein category.

name: Sorghum
notes: Cooked. Whole grain staple across Africa and South Asia.

name: Popcorn
notes: Air-popped. Butter or oil add substantial fat.

name: Steel-cut oats
notes: Cooked. Chewier and slower-cooking than rolled.

name: Freekeh
notes: Cooked. Roasted young wheat with a smoky flavor.

name: Sushi rice
notes: Cooked, seasoned with rice vinegar, salt, and sugar.

name: Arborio rice
notes: Cooked. Short-grain Italian rice; releases starch for creamy risotto.

name: Brazil nut
notes: Raw. One nut delivers a full day of selenium.

name: Chestnut
notes: Roasted. Starchy nut, more like a tuber than other nuts.

name: Sunflower seed butter
notes: Common nut-allergy substitute for peanut butter.

name: Hemp seed
notes: Hulled. Complete protein with omega-3 fats.

name: Poppy seed
notes: Tiny seeds with subtle nutty flavor.

name: Goji berry
notes: Fresh. Most consumed as the dried form.

name: Lime
notes: Raw. Sour citrus, sharper than lemon.

name: Pomegranate
notes: Raw. Juicy red arils, edible seeds inside.

name: Guava
notes: Raw. Highly aromatic; very high in vitamin C.

name: Passion fruit
notes: Raw. Intensely aromatic pulp with edible seeds.

name: Dragon fruit
notes: Raw. Mild taste; striking pink/yellow skin.

name: Lychee
notes: Raw. Fragrant white flesh under a pink shell.

name: Apricot (fresh)
notes: Raw. Smaller and tarter than peach.

name: Jackfruit
notes: Raw, ripe. Unripe jackfruit is used as a meaty texture in savory dishes.

name: Dried cherry
notes: Sweet-tart dried cherries; often sweetened further.

name: Dried blueberry
notes: Sweet, intense blueberry flavor; often sweetened.

name: Sunflower oil
notes: High in linoleic acid; neutral flavor.

name: Safflower oil
notes: Very high smoke point; very neutral.

name: Peanut oil
notes: High smoke point; faint nutty flavor.

name: Walnut oil
notes: Cold-pressed; finish only, not for heat.

name: Palm oil
notes: High in saturated fat; semi-solid at room temperature.

name: Mustard oil
notes: Pungent; central to East Indian and Bengali cooking.

name: Cilantro
notes: Raw. Polarizing fresh herb; key in Latin and South/Southeast Asian cooking.

name: Mint
notes: Raw. Spearmint most common in cooking.

name: Thyme
notes: Raw. Tiny leaves with strong savory aroma.

name: Sage
notes: Often used dried (values here are dried). Fresh leaves are bigger and softer.

name: Tarragon
notes: Often used dried (values here are dried). Fresh has a delicate anise note.

name: Lemongrass
notes: Raw stalk. Citrusy and aromatic; key in Southeast Asian cooking.

name: Brown sugar
notes: White sugar with molasses added back.

name: Powdered sugar
notes: Finely ground sugar with a little cornstarch.

name: Molasses
notes: Byproduct of sugar refining. Robust bitter sweetness.

name: Coconut sugar
notes: Crystallized coconut palm sap; caramel notes.

name: Jaggery
notes: Unrefined sugar from cane or palm sap.

name: White chocolate

notes: Carton style. Much thinner than canned coconut milk.

name: Rice milk
notes: Thinnest and sweetest of the common plant milks.

notes: Full-fat. Much richer than carton coconut milk.

name: Miso (white)
notes: Fermented soybean paste; lightest, sweetest variety.

name: Gochujang
notes: Korean fermented chili paste. Sweet, savory, hot.

name: Harissa
notes: North African chili and spice paste.

name: Tamari
notes: Wheat-free Japanese soy sauce; richer and less salty per spoon.

notes: Tangy fermented condiment with anchovy and tamarind.

name: BBQ sauce
notes: Tomato base, vinegar, smoke; many regional styles.

name: Guacamole
notes: Mashed avocado with lime, onion, cilantro.

name: Sambal oelek
notes: Indonesian crushed chili paste; just chili and salt.

name: Peanut sauce
notes: Peanut, coconut, chili, lime; thick dipping sauce.

name: Curry paste (red, Thai)
notes: Thai red chilies, garlic, lemongrass, galangal, shrimp paste.

name: Lassi (sweet)

name: Buttermilk

name: Goat milk
notes: Whole goat milk. Slightly tangier than cow milk.

name: Sheep milk
notes: Whole sheep milk. Higher in fat and protein than cow milk.

name: Evaporated milk

notes: Deactivated yeast flakes; cheesy nutty flavor.

name: Cocoa powder

name: Coconut (shredded, dried)
notes: Unsweetened dried meat. Sweetened versions add ~20g sugar.

name: Coconut cream
notes: Top layer skimmed from canned coconut milk. Very rich.

name: Black rice
notes: Cooked. Whole-grain rice with deep purple-black bran.

name: Couscous
notes: Cooked. Steamed semolina; technically a tiny pasta.

name: Tomato (canned, whole)
notes: In juice. Lower sodium than canned tomato sauce.

name: Anchovy paste
notes: Concentrated anchovies in oil; used in tiny amounts.

name: Tangerine

name: Blood orange
notes: Raw. Distinctive red flesh with raspberry undertones.

name: Wasabi paste
notes: Most commercial wasabi is dyed horseradish.

name: Roquefort

name: Bread flour

name: Cake flour

name: Semolina

name: Coconut flour
notes: Dried defatted coconut meat ground fine.

name: Oat flour
notes: Finely ground oats. *Gluten-free only if labeled.

name: Chickpea flour (besan)

name: Potato starch

name: Vanilla bean

name: Chocolate chips (milk)

name: Cacao nibs

name: Shortening

name: Niter kibbeh

name: Mace

name: Saffron

name: Sumac

name: Juniper berries

notes: Cooked. Split red lentil (cooks fast and soft).

notes: Cooked. Mung bean or sweet potato starch noodles.

name: Einkorn
notes: Cooked. The oldest cultivated wheat species.

notes: Cooked. Pacific and Caribbean starch fruit.

name: Piloncillo

notes: Sugar alcohol; nearly zero calorie, slight cooling effect.

name: Stevia
notes: Plant-derived sweetener; far sweeter than sugar.

name: Monk fruit sweetener
notes: Extracted from monk fruit; often blended with erythritol.

name: Allulose
notes: Rare sugar; behaves like sucrose but most isn't metabolized.

name: Salt (table)
notes: Refined sodium chloride with anti-caking + often iodine. Mineral, not animal/plant/dairy; filed as plant per the single-group rule (same convention as baking soda).

name: Salt (kosher)
notes: Coarse flaky crystals; lower sodium per teaspoon than table salt due to crystal size. Per-100g sodium is similar.

name: Salt (sea)
notes: Evaporated seawater; trace minerals beyond NaCl. Sodium content essentially identical to table salt.

name: Seasoned salt
notes: Lawry's-style blend: salt + paprika + garlic powder + turmeric + onion powder.

name: Bread crumbs
notes: Plain dry crumbs (not panko). Italian-seasoned variants would carry extra sodium.

name: Graham crackers
notes: Lightly sweetened whole-wheat-flour crackers; honey/molasses sweetened.

name: Margarine (stick)
notes: Hydrogenated vegetable oil + water + emulsifiers. Plant-dominant per the single-group rule even when blended with milk solids.

name: Red wine
notes: Typical dry red, ~12% ABV. Most calories come from ethanol (7 kcal/g).

name: Beer (lager)
notes: Standard American lager, ~4-5% ABV. Carries gluten from barley malt.

name: Cake mix (yellow)
notes: Dry mix; eggs / oil / water added at use. Betty Crocker-style.

name: Pudding mix (vanilla, instant)
notes: Dry instant mix (sugar + modified starch + flavor). Milk added at use.

name: Whipped topping (frozen)
notes: Cool Whip-style. Contains skim milk + light cream; dairy-dominant per the single-group rule.

name: American cheese (slices)
notes: Pasteurized process cheese product. Melts evenly; very salty.

name: Velveeta-style processed cheese
notes: Pasteurized cheese product loaf. Smoother melt than American slices; more carbs from whey/milk solids.

name: Capers
notes: Brined flower buds. Drained values; the brine itself is much saltier.

name: Chicken broth (canned)
notes: Standard reduced-sodium canned/boxed broth. Plain unflavored regular has ~700mg sodium per 100g.

name: Beef broth (canned)
notes: Canned/boxed. Animal-derived per the single-group rule.

name: Cream of mushroom soup (condensed)
notes: Condensed (undiluted) per-100g values. Dairy-dominant per the single-group rule (cream + mushroom — cream is mass-dominant).

name: Coffee (brewed)
notes: Black, unsweetened, no milk. Brewed strength assumes ~60mg caffeine per 100g.

name: Black tea (brewed)
notes: Plain brewed, no milk or sugar. ~20-40mg caffeine per 100g.

name: Orange juice
notes: Fresh-squeezed, unsweetened. Carton varieties similar; calcium-fortified ones add minerals not nutrients tracked here.

name: Apple juice
notes: Clear filtered juice. Cloudy/unfiltered has more fiber.

name: Apple butter
notes: Slow-cooked spiced apple paste. No actual butter — named for its consistency.

name: Biscuit mix (Bisquick-style)
notes: Dry mix; milk/water added at use.

name: Focaccia
notes: Italian flat oven bread, olive-oil enriched.

name: Potato bread
notes: Soft sandwich loaf with potato in dough.

name: Cornbread
notes: Quick bread of cornmeal + wheat flour.

name: Water cracker
notes: Plain crisp cracker for cheese boards.

name: Graham cracker crumbs
notes: Crushed graham crackers for pie crusts.

name: Wheat germ
notes: Nutrient-dense embryo of the wheat kernel.

name: Rye flour
notes: Dark or medium rye; carries gluten.

name: Coffee liqueur (Kahlua-style)

name: Cream liqueur (Baileys-style)
notes: Irish cream liqueur; whiskey + dairy cream.

name: White tea (brewed)
notes: Minimally processed tea leaves. Light caffeine.

name: Oolong tea (brewed)
notes: Partially oxidized tea; caffeine between green/black.

name: Matcha (powder, prepared)
notes: Stone-ground green tea, whisked in water.

name: Chai concentrate

notes: Sugar-free cola with aspartame/sucralose; same caffeine.

notes: Dry mix; eggs/oil/water added at use.

name: Whipped cream (aerosol)
notes: Real dairy whipped cream in a can (Reddi-Whip).

notes: Dry mix; milk added at use.

name: Pudding mix (butterscotch, instant)
notes: Dry mix; milk added at use.

notes: Dry mix; sugar + flavored gelatin powder.
